findings.issue: Suspense has no ErrorBoundary; any non-404 API failure (5xx, network error, malformed JSON thrown in app/src/lib/api.ts:19-25) rejects createAsync with no handler, breaking the render with no user-facing error state.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the route outlet in <ErrorBoundary fallback={...}> alongside Suspense, as the Solid Router docs prescribe, and render a friendly failure page.

findings.issue: Every payload crossing the server/client boundary is typed any (40+ occurrences), so 'strict': true in app/tsconfig.json:12 checks almost nothing; renaming a field in api.ts silently breaks components at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for each loader's return value (HomeData, PokemonPageData, MoveRow, SpeciesCard) in a shared types module and annotate the query wrappers so route components get inference.

findings.issue: Not-found pages render 200; the spec encourages HTTP 404 and SolidStart provides a one-line mechanism for it.
findings.suggestion: Add <HttpStatusCode code={404} /> from @solidjs/start to the NotFound component so unmatched URLs and unknown resources respond correctly.

findings.issue: loadPokemonPageData fans out one fetch per learned move (up to ~190 concurrent requests on a cold cache) even though only the selected game's rows are shown; the results are cached but the first visit to each Pokémon is slow.
findings.suggestion: Either filter moves to the needed version group before fetching, or at least document the deliberate trade-off and cap concurrency; consider fetching move details lazily per selected game.

findings.issue: The <Show when={data()} fallback={<Show when={data() === null}>…}> construct distinguishes loading from not-found via a second nested Show; it works but reads as a trick and is duplicated in four route files.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small <DataOrNotFound data={data()}> component (or a keyed Show) so the loading/null/error states are named and the pattern lives in one place.

findings.issue: The module-level promise cache is unbounded and has no TTL or invalidation; bounded in practice only because the API snapshot is finite.
findings.suggestion: Add a brief comment stating the cache is intentionally process-lifetime and bounded by API size, or implement a simple LRU/TTL if the upstream API grows.

findings.issue: The {name, en} type-reference mapping (with the enName ?? humanize fallback) is constructed five separate times across loadHomeData, loadPokemonPageData, loadMovePageData, loadTypePageData and loadTypeListData.
findings.suggestion: Add a typeRef(name, typeEn) helper next to getTypeNameMap and use it everywhere.

findings.issue: Each <select> sets value on the select and selected on every option; redundant and a known source of hydration quirks.
findings.suggestion: Pick one mechanism — the per-option selected prop is the SSR-safe choice — and drop the select-level value.

summary: This is a faithful, current-spec SolidStart v2 app: the vite/nitro config, query + "use server" placement, preload/createAsync data loading and URL-driven filter state all read like the framework's own docs. The structure is clean — a thin queries.ts server boundary over an api.ts that never leaks to the client — and the card/table components are well scoped. I'd hold the merge for a round of changes: an ErrorBoundary around the Suspense, real types on the payloads instead of pervasive any, an HTTP 404 status on the not-found pages, and slimming the per-move fetch fan-out.
